artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a real or complex Banach space $X$ and a constant $b$ with $1\le b<\infty$, say that $X$ has the $b$-automorphic property if, for every closed subspace $Y\subseteq X$ and every injective bounded linear operator $T\in L(Y,X)$, there exists an injective extension $\widetilde T\in L(X)$ (so $\widetilde T|_Y = T$) satisfying
$$\|\widetilde T\|\,\|\widetilde T^{-1}\| \;\le\; b\,\|T\|\,\|T^{-1}\|,$$
where $\|T^{-1}\|$ denotes the norm of the inverse of $T$ viewed as a map from its range onto $Y$.

For each $n\in\mathbb N$, let $E_n$ be an $n$-dimensional normed space having the $b$-automorphic property (with the same constant $b$, independent of $n$). Let $d(E_n,\ell_2^n)$ denote the Banach–Mazur distance between $E_n$ and the $n$-dimensional Euclidean space $\ell_2^n$, i.e.
$$d(E_n,\ell_2^n)=\inf\{\|S\|\,\|S^{-1}\|: S:E_n\to\ell_2^n \text{ a linear isomorphism}\}.$$

Question: must $\sup_{n\in\mathbb N} d(E_n,\ell_2^n) < \infty$?
